relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: entered the Académie de Genève in November, 1835. There he remained for four years, of which the first three were passed in the Faculty of Philosophy, and the last in that of Science.

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: During a part of this period he studied under Jean Humbert

relations.subject: Jean Humbert
relations.evidence: Jean Humbert, who (like Freytag, with whom he afterwards pursued his studies) was a pupil of the great French Orientalist Sylvestre de Sacy.

relations.subject: Freytag
relations.evidence: Freytag, with whom he afterwards pursued his studies) was a pupil of the great French Orientalist Sylvestre de Sacy.

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: In the Autumn of 1840 he left Geneva for the University of Bonn, where he was inscribed in the Philosophical Faculty on October 30 of that year, and where he remained till the Summer of 1843, when he received his doctor's degree

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: He at once began to read Arabic with Freytag

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: He at once began to read Arabic with Freytag and Sanskrit with Lassen

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: At a later period of his residence at Bonn he read Arabic both with Freytag and Gildemeister

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: In 1847 was published at St. Petersburg Hemachandra's Sanskrit Dictionary, the Abhidana chintamani, in the pro- duction of which Dr. Rieu collaborated with Böhtlingk

relations.subject: Charles Rieu
relations.evidence: In the same year he entered the British Museum, in which for nearly half a century he was one of the most zealous and indispensable officers.

relations.subject: Léon Feer
relations.evidence: In 1864 he was appointed to a Paris professorship, succeeding M. Foucaux in the Chair of Tibetan originally created for the Bibliothèque Nationale and transferred in 1865 to the École des Langues Orientales.

relations.subject: Léon Feer
relations.evidence: He afterwards (1869) held a lectureship in Tibetan and Mongol at the Collège de France.

relations.subject: Léon Feer
relations.evidence: In 1872 M. Feer entered the MS. Department of the Bibliothèque Nationale... In 1900 he was appointed Conservateur-Adjoint
